featured_reviews.name: aditi shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Craved for chinese. Saw this place while exploring. We always fear on trying new places. I have never feared for trying out new places. I don't regret my decision of ordering from this place. I ordered starters and main course.

Starters:
Paneer manchurian: They provide you paneer manchurian in 2 different containers. Paneer was perfectly cooked, the only thing was the salt was on a higher base. Little less salt would have made it an amazing dish. The food has a lot of oil. The manchurian was spicy and good. If you are not a spicy eater, i would suggest please request the hotel to make it less spicy. I personally enjoyed as I'm a spice lover.

Main course:
Rice combo meal: They give you fried rice with manchurian gravy. They have the since of spice and cuisine. Not all restuarants have that. The blend of vegetables with the rice and masala, couldn't have been better.
Thousand island Noodles: I ordered thousand island noodles and it comes in 2 colors as you can see it in the photo. Plain and schezwan. They also provide you with a gravy. The food was impeccable and superbly made. They know how much to cook and how exactly to mix the spices with the veggies. Good job on the cooking part.
In all I didn't regret my try out experience here. Much recommend. TRY!!

featured_reviews.name: Vivek Vetal
featured_reviews.review_text:
I recently visited Persian Darbar in Byculla after hearing a lot of buzz around it. Given its reputation and the constant crowd outside, my expectations were naturally quite high. However, my overall experience was somewhat mixed.

To start with the positives — the ambience is genuinely good. The interiors are well done, with a spacious seating layout and a proper family-restaurant vibe. It feels grand and lively, which explains the heavy footfall. Do note that the place is almost always crowded. If you’re planning to visit, I would strongly recommend booking a table in advance or reaching a little early to avoid the long waiting time.

Coming to the food — I tried the Moroccan Kebab, Murgh Lebnani, Murgh Zafrani Tikka, Bihari Boti, and Chicken Biryani. Honestly, I found most of the dishes average. The taste and quality were mediocre, nothing extraordinary— the kind of flavour you can easily find at many other restaurants on the same street. Given the hype around the place, I expected something more distinctive or memorable. The Moroccan Kebab and Murgh variants were okay, but they didn’t stand out in terms of spice balance or uniqueness. The Bihari Boti was a bit undercooked.

The Chicken Biryani was comparatively better than the rest — flavorful, well-cooked rice, and properly spiced. It was the highlight of the meal for me.

Service, however, was quite slow — probably because of the constant rush. Staff were polite, but you’ll need some patience.

Overall, I felt the place is slightly overhyped. If you’re a hardcore foodie looking for exceptional flavours, you can skip it. If you do visit, go with limited expectations about the taste and focus more on the ambience and overall experience rather than culinary excellence.

featured_reviews.name: Suryaprakash Barnwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College, Dadar definitely attracts a huge crowd. We reached around 2:15 PM and still had to wait close to 40 minutes in the queue before getting served, which itself shows how popular the place is.

The location is definitely a plus point since it’s close to Dadar Beach. The highlight for me was the crispy chura, which added a unique crunch and gave the vada pav a different texture compared to regular stalls.

However, the overall experience felt a bit overrated for the wait and pricing. The service was slow, there was no extra chutney or extra chura provided, and the vada pavs were simply wrapped in paper and handed over. Since everything is pre-made, there’s almost no scope for customization in terms of chutney or spice level like you usually get at local vendors. Personally, I also found the taste slightly too sweet.

The pricing is ₹35 for a single vada pav and ₹140 for four pieces, which feels almost double compared to many other local vendors offering similar or even better taste.

Overall, it’s worth trying once for the hype and experience, but personally I don’t think the taste and service justify waiting more than 40 minutes when there are plenty of local places serving equally good vada pav with faster service, better customization, and more value for money.

featured_reviews.name: Shreyash Bidave
featured_reviews.review_text:
After taking blessings at Shree Siddhivinayak Temple, a visit to Ashok Vada Pav is almost a ritual for food lovers. The vada pav here is served hot and fresh, with a perfectly crispy vada, soft pav, and flavorful chutneys that make every bite memorable.
One of the best experiences is to take a parcel and head towards Dadar Chowpatty. Sitting by the sea, enjoying the view and cool breeze while eating this iconic vada pav creates a combination that's hard to beat. The joy of having Ashok Vada Pav with the sea view is something truly special.
The long queue outside the stall speaks for itself. Just looking at the crowd, you can tell how popular this place is. It's not famous without reason—the taste, consistency, and quality have made it a favorite among Mumbaikars and tourists alike for years.
If you're in Mumbai, this is a must-try street food experience. For many people, Ashok Vada Pav isn't just a snack; it's a part of Mumbai's food culture and one of the most famous vada pav destinations in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Arun
featured_reviews.review_text:
I finally tried the famous Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College. Here is my honest take:

The Good part:
• Location: It is located very close to Dadar Beach. It’s nice to grab your order and go for a short walk by the sea.
• Texture: The combination of the vada with the crispy "chura" is definitely interesting and adds a nice crunch.

The Not-So-Good:
• The Wait: Be prepared to stand in line. It took me between 20-30 minutes just to get served.
• Taste & Customization: Because the Vada Pavs are pre-made, there is hardly any room for customization. Unlike other local shops where you can adjust the chutney to your liking, here you get what you get. Personally, I found the taste a bit too salty and sweet for my palate.

The Price:
• ₹30 per piece
• ₹60 for a plate (2 Vada Pavs)

Verdict: While it’s not "bad," I don't think it is worth a 30-minute wait, especially when other local spots offer better customization.

featured_reviews.name: Naresh Shirodkar
featured_reviews.review_text:
In a city that runs on speed, spice, and soul, some places don’t just serve food, they become emotion. Ashok Vada Pav near Kirti College is exactly that kind of institution, where generations have stood shoulder to shoulder, waiting for that one perfect bite.
What makes their vada pav truly iconic is the balance. The batata vada is crisp on the outside, soft and flavourful inside, with just the right hint of garlic and spice. The pav is always fresh, lightly toasted, and acts as the perfect carrier without overpowering the star.
But the real magic lies in their chutney game. That signature dry garlic chutney hits instantly with a bold, smoky spice, while the fried green chillies on the side elevate the entire experience. It’s not just heat, it’s character, the kind that lingers and keeps you coming back.
And then comes the cult favourite, the chura pav. Buttery, spicy, slightly messy, and absolutely addictive. The crushed vada mixed with chutneys and masala, soaked into the pav, creates a texture and flavour bomb that feels indulgent in the most Mumbai way possible. Crisp edges, soft centres, and that unmistakable street-style richness.
Being a true Dadarkar, I’ve grown up eating this vada pav, and what’s incredible is how the taste has remained exactly the same over the years, still the best vada pav, hands down.
There’s a legacy here that you can actually taste. Started decades ago and now run by the next generation, Ashok Vada Pav has become a landmark in Dadar’s food scene. It has seen college crowds, office rush, late-night hunger, and everything in between, yet the consistency remains untouched. No unnecessary reinvention, just doing the basics exceptionally well, every single time. The vibe is classic Mumbai, fast-moving queues, minimal waiting despite the crowd, and an energy that feels alive. You don’t come here for luxury, you come here for authenticity.
Ashok Vada Pav isn’t just food, it’s a ritual, a memory, and for many, a weekly craving that never fades.
Simple, iconic, and absolutely unbeatable. 🌶️🔥

name: Love in Langos
description:
Langos is a typical Hungarian food. Nowadays it is a deep fried flatbread, but in the past it was made of the last bits of the bread-dough and baked at the front of a brick or clay oven, to be served hot as the breakfast of the bread-baking day.
Up to the mid 20th century, bread was baked once a week due to the cost of heating up the large oven and the lengthy proces. Because the bread loaf, typical to Hungary, was 6 to 10 pounds each, traditionally they used to bake smaller (1-2 pounds) "cipó" rolls for the evening and the next day. The name lángos (literally meaning "flamed") comes from baking these flat breads.

Love in Lagos - Cafe serves both baked and Fried versions. Lets try some.

It instantly reminded me of the Hungarian food I had back in Budapest, which I wasn’t expecting to find here at all.

Also, the menu was a bit confusing at first (at least for us 😅), but the owner was such a warm and helpful person. He took the time to explain everything and helped us figure out what to order, which made the whole experience even better.

Kurtos which is a traditional speciality of Hungary is one of the main highlights of this place . Cylindrical in shape crisp on the outside and a savoury filling inside. Our all time favourite here is pesto Mushroom and Chipotle Veggies variant of Kurtos.

Another speciality of this place is Langos which  is a deep fried flat bread topped with cheese , veggies and baked to perfection. This cranberry Langos is our all time favourite and one should definitely go for this one whenever out here.

Lastly do give a try to cinnamon and sugar Trdelnik Which is a chef  special dessert. The balance of every ingredient in this one is impeccable.

This Diwali they have also come up with some food combo offers which will include all best dishes of the house. Make sure you definitely add this one to the top of your food bucket list.

featured_reviews.review_text:
A Pure Vegetarian Place located on the ground floor of Atria Mall, Worli. Bombay Street with all the food and grafittis inside the wall related to Mumbai's street food and culture is a cool place to hang out with family and friends. The food menu has varieties of local Mumbai's street and city's staple food and some of the North Indian varieties from the mains to gorge on to.
Well, its all fusion, nothing authentic in particular. Just like they have some fusion varieties in Dosa, Vada pav and sandwiches apart from the Mumbai's local authentic ones.
And I really loved hogging -
- Chat Platter
-Gini Dosa
- Spicy Tikka Panini Sandwich- it had tandoori paneer rolled in flat bread with chutney
- Bibimap- Fragrance rice served with exotic veg Bibimap from the mains that you should definitely try.
The rice tasted perfect with the special gravy that it was served with and that too having with exotic veggies was a win win.
Dessert- All ends that ends well. Hence a sweet note to end my good eating time here with-Gulab jamun
Moongdal halwa
With all heavy stomach, I had a lovely time here eating all fusion and Mumbai's best street food. Its a great place to hog especially who are die hard fan of street food.

featured_reviews.name: Jatin Shah
featured_reviews.review_text:
Atria Mall is where one finds loads of options to choose from in terms of having their meal and it is home to Bombay Street Co. - paradise for vegetarians. Located at Level 0 the place gives you an experience of a chaat bazaar in a sophisticated environment. And that's where I believe Bombay Street Co. scores against other restaurants. Providing the best of street food in a hygienic environment. Now since the restaurant is a pure veg restaurant, it shall have its own flipside of attracting large groups and families and it tends to get a little noisy. But if one is fine with it, believe it's the place to head to.

Talking about what all I tried here -

We called for couple of starters - Youger Poppers and Veg Tandoori Platter. Of the two, I would personally recommend all to try the Younger Poppers, quite different from the jalapeno cheese poppers. In this it's a combination of capsicum, cheese crushed with papadam. Tandoori Platter is a serving of kebabs - Tandoori Aloo, Paneer Tikka, Tandoori Mushrooms and Tandoori Baby Corn. A bit of work needed specially for the mushrooms and baby corn, they weren't grilled enough. Aloo was nice and so was paneer.

Along with food, we ordered for couple of drinks - Mint Mojito and Spice Guava Chilli. Both drinks quite basic but refreshing, solves the purpose. Some work can be done towards the presentation of drinks perhaps. Moving to the mains, as mentioned earlier the place offers scrumptious street food in a good ambience. So was excited to try the Pizza Dosa straight from Anna Ki Galli. Superb fusion of 2 dishes. Believe this and Gini dosa as usual would be the regular favorites of all at this restaurant. Something one should not miss.

Last but not the least, tried couple of desserts - Gulab Jamun with Vanilla and Jalebi with Rabdi. Both were recommending and trying basis preference taste and choice. Mind you, one gets a plate full of Jalebi so you may need a few to share the plate. But tastes heavenly, so does the combination of gulab jamun with Vanilla Ice-cream scoop.

All-in-all a paradise for pure veg food eaters who prefer going to places which don't serve non veg food. And ofcourse street food with a great combo of taste and hygiene. Do pay a visit when possible.

featured_reviews.name: Bhavin Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Bombay Street Co. is a finest vegetarian restaurant in Atria Mall at Worli. The ambience is decent with mumbai theme decor where vintage photos of mumbai places framed nicely and hanged on the wall adds grace to the place. The menu is crafted wisely by keeping trending food delicacies according to mumbai peoples taste. This place serves northindian, southindian, chinese, chaats along with pizza, pasta and more.
Out of many tempting food dishes Few selected and tried 👇🏻
🔹️ Assorted Tandoor Platter - this one is a treat for tandoor lovers .... soft paneer tikkas, Long Babycorns marinated in tikka masala and Baby potatoes cooked perfectly with indian spices along with inhouse salad was awesome and flavoursome.
🔹️ Gini Dosa - A South indian preparation of dosa stuffed with paneer, cheese, capsicum and onions was an outstanding fusion dosa that tasted cheesy and yummy.
🔹️Chopper Rice - An amazing Chinese main course of fried rice, noodles, manchurian balls and exotic veggies gravies ... All in one plate was superb in presentation, taste as well as quantity.
🔹️ Kesar Jalebi - Hot and crispy Jalebis topped with dryfruits was succulent and luscious.

Even tried few mocktails like Watermelon mojito and Cosmo rita ( cranberry and orange flavoured) which were chilled and refreshing to the last sip. Also tasted its Oreo Frappe - a thick shake that was made of chocolate icecream, milk and oreo was awesome in taste too.
Overall the food was prepared perfectly having good taste and presentation. Even the service was quick and the staff were well mannered and polite. A excellent vegetarian place to dine with family and friends.

featured_reviews.name: NomNom Mumbaikar
featured_reviews.review_text:
Being a Mumbai based person we always get fascinated and mesmerised by looking at the historical properties in Mumbai. We all love to gaze at the old architecture and the vintage things of the city. So I happen to drop by this restaurant and the name says it all "Bombay Street Co" and it seems that they love Mumbai as much as we do. It's a vegetarian restaurant. It’s a nice little cosy place in the vicinity of Worli. When you enter this place you will see two different architects on the wall. One side shows the life in Mumbai and the other side gives you a vintage look. The setup is very nice and subtle with not so loud music around which I feel is a nice thing. The ambience is very nice.

When it comes to food it’s really amazing. They offer Bombay street style food with a modern touch to it and I bet you are going to love it. And they have so many amazing options that you might end up ordering too many dishes. So I had gone with my friends and we had ordered few moctails and other dishes. So here’s the list of moctails and dishes that we had ordered.In mocktails we ordered watermelon mojito, oreo frappe, peach ice tea and spiced guava chilli . Spiced guava chilli was my absolute favourite. We also tried their cheesey and beany nachos, Kung Pao cottage cheese, Bibimbap. So basically Bibimbap is a Korean rice dish which is a mix of various ingredients. In desserts we  ordered sizzling brownie and gulab jamun with vanilla ice cream. And trust me we were too stuffed to move.

We had a very good experience visiting Bombay Street co. The staff was very friendly and they also helped us in selecting their signature dishes.

Cheesy Comfort with a Charming Twist!

Visited Say Cheese, Parel with friends and had a really satisfying experience. The menu is a dream come true for cheese lovers—and it didn’t disappoint!

We tried their Chocolate Milkshake, which was thick, creamy, and beautifully presented with chocolate drizzle. It wasn’t overly sweet and felt refreshing after the heavy mains.

The Cheese Grilled Sandwich came loaded with grated cheese and crunchy veggies. Served with chips, it made for a comforting, satisfying bite. The sandwich was crisp on the outside and generously filled—perfect for a cheesy indulgence!

Next up was their Mac N Cheese Pizza, which was the star of the meal. A fusion of pasta and pizza, it had a lovely cheesy crust, soft macaroni topping, and a good balance of seasoning. Ideal for those who enjoy quirky, fusion food.

The ambiance was cozy and aesthetic—floral ceiling lights, green-tiled flooring, and comfortable wooden seating gave it a warm café vibe. Great for both casual hangouts and Insta-worthy pictures.

Why not 5 stars? Slightly longer wait time during peak hours and the food was a bit on the heavier side (expected, considering the cheese-centric theme). But overall, it’s worth visiting for a cheesy, feel-good meal with friends.

Must-try: Mac N Cheese Pizza & Chocolate Shake!
